note_tweet.text:
It could be vastly underestimated how much human expertise is needed to diffuse the benefits of AI to the long-tail of knowledge work. I think more data companies should figure out this branding, where experts help AI companies understand how to improve the tools that make them more effective, rather than replaced.

Some jobs will be replaced for sure, but I think a lot of knowledge work is deeply interpersonal, messy, and context driven in a way where AI adoption will be a productivity boon to existing employees. We are seeing this with the demand for SWEs today.

This rebrand will serve the AI industry writ large very well, but goes against the RSI narratives of the labs as "ASI will replace all knowledge work." In some ways, the difference is more philosophical about "what is the nature of work." I believe knowledge work is much more human than the evals give credit for, and this will make diffusion take a long time. Seems like Mercor can be at the center of this diffusion puzzle.

Disclosure: Yes, I advise Mercor on trying to realize this puzzle, as I think it's super interesting.

article.plain_text:
Scientific discovery is a lengthy process that can take decades to provide relief for those suffering from rare diseases. Early and sustained investments in research on these conditions can make the difference between life and death for these individuals. The National Institutes of Health (NIH has supported investigations on fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP) in order to help patients with this disease, which is an ultra-rare genetic disease characterized by devastating, abnormal bone formation in soft tissues such as muscle, tendons and ligaments, causing limited movement, deformities, severe disability, and early death.
Beginning in 1994, NIH’s National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases (NIAMS) supported research into the genetic, molecular and cellular basis of FOP. More recently, NIAMS has funded numerous research teams and universities around the nation to explore promising therapeutic approaches. This foundational knowledge has been leveraged by pharmaceutical companies to develop therapies for the disease.  As a result of these efforts, in August and September of this year, the U.S. Food and Drug Agency (FDA) announced approvals for the second and third drugs for this patient group.
Pasatru (garetosmab-grts) and Atebrioz (zilurgisertib) block the activation of a faulty receptor, called activin A receptor-type 1 (ACVR1), that contributes to abnormal bone growth in people with FOP. Pasatru is an antibody that blocks binding of activin A to the faulty receptor. In a 56-week clinical study, participants taking Pasatru only developed up to two new areas of bone growth, compared with 19 new areas of bone growth in the placebo group. Atebrioz is a daily pill that blocks the activity of that same faulty receptor. In a 24-week study, patients taking Atebrioz experienced an average decrease of 3.2 cm3 in measured abnormal bone volume, while those taking a placebo had an average increase of 24.6 cm3.
Great strides have been made in developing therapeutic treatments to help block ACVR1-induced bone growth. That said, the research continues and NIAMS will continue to support research to improve the lives of people with FOP and other rare bone diseases.

L’intelligence artificielle avance très vite. On l’a déjà vu : cela implique des risques réels pour notre sécurité collective. 
                             
Notre travail pour developper nos technologies doit aussi être celui de l’anticipation et de la maîtrise de ses risques.

J’ai réuni à Paris et en visio une cinquantaine d’acteurs : chefs d’État et de gouvernement, dirigeants des plus grands laboratoires d’IA, chercheurs et experts.

Le constat est partagé. Il faut agir ensemble. Nous avons obtenu des engagements de tous autour de trois priorités : mieux évaluer de façon indépendante et publique les risques des modèles les plus avancés, mieux partager les alertes en cas d’incident grave et responsabiliser les acteurs qui développent des modèles.

Notre ambition est claire : faire de l’IA un progrès pour tous, avec une sécurité garantie par l’engagement de chacun.
